goal: As ClearFlow's purchasing agent, evaluate three supplier bids for 15 MRO line items across three requisitions, benchmark them against SF open-data MRO purchases, and decide between single-source and category split award under a $35K cap and a 3-week OSHA safety deadline. Deliverables: price_benchmark_analysis.csv, a three-sheet bid evaluation workbook, POs on the provided template, and a decision memo to Sarah Chen.
delivered: All four deliverables: price_benchmark_analysis.csv (72 commodity rows built from the downloaded SF dataset), bid_evaluation_workbook.xlsx (Line Item Comparison, Weighted Evaluation, Split-Award Analysis), purchase_orders_split_award.xlsx (PO-2025-0112A to Pacific for Electrical+Safety, PO-2025-0112B to TriState for Plumbing) and procurement_decision_memorandum.docx recommending that split.
what_went_wrong: The agent got the mechanics right (benchmark CSV, file set, cap check) but made shallow or wrong judgment calls. It forced specialized items (LED hazardous-location fixture, metering pump, HDPE pipe, chlorine detector) onto broad commodity medians instead of flagging 'No Benchmark'. It treated early-pay discounts as face-value dollars with no annualized/NPV analysis, and never dollarized Pacific's extra pump warranty, so plumbing went to TriState over a $14.50 difference. It never converted 14-21 business days to calendar weeks against the 3-week OSHA window, and PO-0112B shows $0 freight despite TriState's $385 FOB-origin charge, with no category subtotals in PO-0112A. Its OSHA mitigation in the memo is limited to asking for written confirmation.

failed_items.why: All 15 items and suppliers are consolidated correctly, but specialized items were mapped to generic medians (LED fixture vs ELECTRICAL MATERIALS $9.31, metering pump/HDPE vs PLUMBING $10.62) and flagged Above Benchmark; zero 'No Benchmark' flags, although the agent considered that option in its reasoning at step 27.

Both scenarios and the freight thresholds are modeled, but the TCO columns are Base, Freight and Conditional Discounts only: early-pay discounts are applied at face value with no NPV, and Pacific's extended pump warranty has no value in the TCO.

Outputs call TriState's '14–21 business days' a safety risk but never convert it to ~2.8–4.2 calendar weeks against the 3-week OSHA window stated in TASK_INSTRUCTIONS, and never call the 14-day lower bound borderline.

PO-2025-0112A shows a single 14,717.75 subtotal with no Electrical/Safety breakout, and PO-2025-0112B shows SHIPPING/HANDLING 0 although supplier_bid_proposals lists TriState freight as an estimated $385 flat rate, FOB Origin; the $385 is mentioned only in remarks.

Dollar discounts ($1,013.66 Apex, $664.55 Pacific) are correct, but there is no days-early calculation or annualized return (~31% / ~49% APR) and no statement that the discounts are high-return opportunities.

Warranty enters only as a 1-5 score. Pacific's extra pump warranty is never valued against the $1,198–$1,345 pump price or the diaphragm failures cited in PR-2025-0042, and plumbing was awarded to TriState over a $14.50 difference.

TriState (14–21 business days) is awarded plumbing, yet the memo offers only written delivery confirmation: no not-to-exceed date or penalty clause, no backup supplier, and no note that Apex's 10–14 days could be tight.

subagent_notes: One subagent (step 4) extracted requisitions, bids and the PO template structure and reported back. That helped with input parsing. The analytical gaps came from the root agent's own modeling choices.
